digest.component_or_area: dependency advisory scanning and CI gating
propositions: A committed lock pins transitive dependencies, causing any future advisory on that pinned version to fail the gating pip-audit job on all in-flight changes regardless of whether they touch the dependency map
The retry logic in the pip-audit job only retries database-unreachable failures, making recheck a time-wasting first instinct that cannot clear real findings
constraint-dependencies can only narrow an existing constraint set and returns UNSATISFIABLE as expected output, which is routinely misinterpreted as proof that an upgrade is impossible
override-dependencies is the correct instrument to replace an offending requirement from an upstream cap, but overrides must carry a REMOVE-WHEN condition or they outlive their justification silently

The Gerrit verify lane should block on an advisory only when the change touches the dependency map, not on all changes, so that non-dependency work does not suffer red status for lock-related advisories
A scheduled main-branch run must fail visibly when an outstanding advisory exists on a pinned dependency, routing to an owner via a deduplicated ticket rather than silently remaining red
